transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-04-30
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Lina Morales (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Elliot Chen (CTO, GranitePay), Priya Rao (SRE Lead), Marcus Lee (ML Infra), Dana Park (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Align on SLO hypothesis and traffic emulation plan for POC; define TTFT and TPOT targets for p95/p99; agree on data samples, benchmark modes, and deliverables.

[00:00] Lina: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro, I'm Lina from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. Samir is our SE and will take us through latency tradeoffs and benchmark plan.
[00:18] Elliot: Hey, thanks for setting this up. We'll be pretty focused on latency under load and the tail, and how that maps to customer experience.
[00:28] Samir: cool, so agenda—1) success criteria, 2) workload sizing and traffic emulation, 3) benchmark modes and measurement plan, 4) timeline and next steps. does that sound ok?
[00:36] Priya: yep that's perfect. also want to briefly cover security boundary for the pilot.
[00:41] Lina: noted. quick round of roles—Elliot you said CTO, Priya runs SRE, Marcus is infra, Dana PM—ok.

[00:58] Samir: i'll start with the SLO framing. Our standard approach is to define a primary user-facing SLO and a secondary unit-economics SLO. Primary usually is TTFT — time to first token — because for interactive chat that's what customers perceive. Secondary is TPOT — total per-token latency or sometimes people call it TPT — the per-token generation speed, which influences throughput and cost.
[01:22] Marcus: small point — in our docs we sometimes measure "first-byte" which is similar but slightly different, is that a problem?
[01:30] Samir: not a problem, we can map first-byte to TTFT with a small offset. we should standardize on naming for the POC though. we'd prefer TTFT and TPOT to avoid confusion.

[01:45] Priya: from SRE perspective we're thinking p95 and p99 targets. for interactive payments flows we target p95 < 400ms and p99 < 900ms for TTFT. does that sound realistic?
[01:58] Samir: depends on model size and whether you want hosted or dedicated. if you run a 7B quantized on dedicated GPUs, hitting p95~200-300ms is doable; for p99 you'd want more careful batching and prefix cache. but if you route to a large 70B model, it's much higher.
[02:16] Elliot: we plan to serve two modalities—short responses for transaction confirmation (~20 tokens) and longer responses for dispute explanations (~120 tokens). How do we weigh TTFT vs TPOT?
[02:28] Samir: we'll propose a weighted SLO: 70% traffic weight on short path (TTFT priority) and 30% on long path (TPOT also matters). for acceptance we'll define a composite: weighted p95 and weighted p99.

[02:45] Dana: can you show an example acceptance matrix?
[02:48] Samir: sure, sketching verbally:
- Short path (70%): TTFT p95 < 350ms, p99 < 850ms
- Long path (30%): TTFT p95 < 450ms, p99 < 1.5s; TPOT median < 20ms/token, p95 < 35ms/token
Weighted SLO: compute quantile per path and combine by traffic weight.

[03:22] Priya: ok that seems like a starting point. do we need to include cold-start and cache-warm phases?
[03:28] Samir: yes we'll run two benchmark phases: cold (empty KV cache, first 30 minutes), warm (steady state after prefix-KV cache warmed). we'll also run a burst test for tail behavior.

[03:42] Elliot: what about concurrency and batching? our peak concurrency today is ~120 qps for the short path but bursts up to 450 qps for promotions.
[03:52] Samir: good, we'll emulate three modes: steady (120 qps), burst (spike to 450 qps for 3-5 minutes), and tail-sweep (long tail patterns with diurnal spikes). each run will report TTFT p50/p95/p99 and TPOT distribution.

[04:12] Lina: note — from pricing and pilot sizing we'll need to propose Dedicated pool sizing for that burst profile and fallback behavior to hosted if you exceed reserved capacity.

[04:25] Priya: on the security side — we require SOC2, SAML SSO for console, audit logs, and KMS integration for key management. can you confirm Redwood Private or Dedicated meets this?
[04:38] Samir: yes, Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs. our private control plane option covers stricter requirements. we'll attach SOC2 and architecture diagrams to the follow-up.

[04:54] Marcus: for the POC we'll probably want to run in a VPC peered environment or use your Private agent. which is faster to stand up?
[05:01] Samir: VPC peering to Redwood Dedicated is usually faster—couple of hours to configure peering and IAM roles if your infra team is ready. Private on-prem is heavier. for a 2-week pilot dedicated is recommended.

[05:14] Elliot: ok that fits our timeline. we want pilot in mid-May — is that feasible?
[05:19] Lina: yes, if we get sample traces and sign a pilot order by May 5, we can target test start May 12.

[05:27] Samir: going back to measurement, we'll collect token-level timing and request-level traces. two critical derived metrics: TTFT per request (ms), and TPOT (ms/token). we'll compute p50/p95/p99 per run and also report per-model and per-route breakdowns.

[05:47] Priya: about sampling — we can't share full PII traffic. we will provide anonymized payloads; can you confirm synthetic rewrites preserve size and token distributions?
[05:57] Samir: yes our emulation tooling can replay the tokenized sequence shapes and distribution while redacting PII. we only need token count and typical prompt shapes to match latency characteristics.

[06:08] Dana: how do you handle deterministic randomness — e.g., different seeds change token count?
[06:13] Samir: we parameterize the generator to sample from your token-length histogram, and we can fix seeds for reproducibility. we'll also add small jitter to mimic real network variance.

[06:26] Elliot: what's the expected noise in the TPOT metric across runs?
[06:30] Samir: depends on hardware and contention. for a controlled dedicated pool we usually see TPOT median variance <5% across identical runs; p99 is more sensitive to background noise, which is why we do multiple runs and report confidence intervals.

[06:48] Priya: you mentioned fallback policies earlier — can you detail behavior if Dedicated saturates?
[06:54] Samir: yes we can configure smart routing: if dedicated capacity is maxed, route new requests to a lower-cost hosted tier or a smaller model variant; we also support graceful degradation like short-path truncation and preemptive retries.

[07:10] Marcus: curious about KV cache — we've seen "KV cash" typed in older notes — how big a factor is prefix caching to TTFT?
[07:19] Samir: huge. if you can cache common prefixes, TTFT can drop by 30-60% for long-context workloads. for GranitePay's short confirmations it's less critical, but for dispute explanations it helps a lot.

[07:32] Dana: for the benchmark we'll need to define sample sizes for p99 verification. what's your recommended sample size?
[07:37] Samir: to estimate p99 with reasonable confidence, aim for at least 10k samples per path per run; for 99th percentile CI narrowness we recommend 20k if feasible. we'll propose an exact sampling table based on your QPS.

[07:55] Priya: lowering cost is also a goal — can Redwood provide quantization recommendations?
[07:59] Samir: yes we'll include model/quantization profiles. e.g., 8-bit quant for 13B can deliver similar TPOT to FP16 at lower cost but slightly higher median; we will test model variants and report quality regressions if any.

[08:14] Elliot: for SLO acceptance — is it pass/fail or graded?
[08:17] Samir: usually a pass/fail against acceptance criteria, but we also provide a risk register showing where targets are missed and mitigation (scale, caching, smaller model, config).

[08:29] Lina: quick checkpoint — agreed deliverables: (1) Redwood provides benchmark tooling & run plan, (2) GranitePay provides anonymized traces, (3) Redwood shares SOC2 + architecture, (4) set up dedicated pilot. all agreed?
[08:43] Group: yes.

[08:50] Samir: now i'll outline the benchmark matrix. three modes:
- Mode A: Steady-state run at 120 qps for 30 minutes (cache warm)
- Mode B: Burst run: ramp to 450 qps for 5 minutes, observe tail and saturation behavior
- Mode C: Cold-start run: empty cache, run long-tail pattern for 1 hour to capture cache-heat dynamics
For each mode we'll report TTFT p50/p95/p99, TPOT median/p95/p99, and resource utilization (GPU % and mem).

[09:30] Marcus: what about tokenization variance? we need to ensure synthetic prompts match your tokenizer's token counts.
[09:36] Samir: we'll tokenize your sample prompts with the target model tokenizer and use that token histogram. this is why the sample traces are important.

[09:47] Priya: any recommendations on model choice for initial pilot? we want low latency but acceptable quality for dispute explanations.
[09:54] Samir: a 13B quantized model on dedicated GPUs often hits the sweet spot. if you need better quality, 33/34B is next step but expect TTFT to be 2-3x higher unless aggressive caching. we can test both as part of the POC.

[10:09] Elliot: cost question — can you ballpark cost for 2-week dedicated pilot sized for our burst profile?
[10:16] Lina: rough order: a minimal dedicated pool sized for 450 qps bursts for 2 weeks with autoscaling buffer is ~$25k-$40k depending on instance type and burst capacity. i'll send a firm quote after sizing with Samir's run results.

[10:29] Priya: acceptable range, thanks. on instrumentation — what logs/metrics do you expose so our SREs can correlate with app-side traces?
[10:36] Samir: we expose per-request IDs, token-level timings, model-version, routing path, and per-GPU telemetry. we can push metrics to your Prometheus or provide access to Redwood Console dashboards.

[10:49] Dana: how will we compute the weighted SLO? do you provide tooling?
[10:52] Samir: we provide scripts to compute weighted quantiles from raw traces. we'll also commit a spreadsheet with formulas.

[11:00] Lina: logistics — sample trace export: Elliot, you mentioned you can deliver 14 days of sampled traces. what's the format?
[11:07] Elliot: we can produce JSONL with anonymized prompts, token counts, timestamps, route labels. we need an S3 bucket path to drop them.

[11:15] Samir: perfect, we'll provide an upload manifest and tokenization tool. please include at least 2k short-path and 500 long-path samples as minimum. ideally more.

[11:28] Priya: regarding privacy — are uploads encrypted at rest?
[11:31] Samir: yes S3 server-side encryption, plus we support client-side encryption and KMS keys if you prefer.

[11:40] Marcus: on the measurement side, how do you handle retries and timeouts in computing TTFT? do retries inflate p99?
[11:47] Samir: we compute TTFT on the first successful attempt; retries are annotated and excluded from primary SLO but included in a secondary reliability metric. timeouts are recorded separately.

[11:58] Dana: about fallbacks — if we degrade to a smaller model for cost, what is the expected delta in TPOT and token quality?
[12:05] Samir: smaller model reduces TPOT but may change semantics. we'll run a quality regression on your prompt set and provide a tradeoff table: quality-loss vs cost savings vs latency improvement.

[12:18] Priya: timeline recap?
[12:21] Lina: propose sign pilot order by 2025-05-05, samples delivered by 2025-05-05, bench runs week of 2025-05-12, results and remediation plan by 2025-05-16.

[12:33] Elliot: that timeline works if we can prioritize trace export.

[12:38] Samir: technical note — for the burst run we'll instrument GPU-level profiling; that will help us determine whether latency is queuing or model execution bound.

[12:49] Marcus: nice. do you provide guidance on autoscaler settings?
[12:52] Samir: yes we'll recommend autoscale thresholds, cooldowns, and burst buffer size based on run results.

[13:00] Priya: any blocker for sample size? we can provide more than 14 days but will prioritize last 14 days.
[13:06] Elliot: we'll prep and anonymize. Marcus will own the export.

[13:12] Dana: legal/contract note — we'll need a short MSA addendum for the pilot with data processing terms.
[13:18] Lina: our legal can send a one-page pilot addendum. I'll include that in next steps.

[13:26] Samir: experimental detail — we'll run each mode 3 times and compute median and CI. if the p99 is close to target, we'll do an A/B test on routing fallback to measure impact.

[13:40] Priya: question — are we going to measure user-perceived latency end-to-end or just service-side?
[13:45] Samir: both. you'll get service-side TTFT/TPOT and we recommend you capture client-side first-byte too; we'll provide request-id for correlation.

[13:58] Elliot: who should we cc on uploads and legal thread?
[14:02] Lina: cc me and Samir; i'll loop in legal: legal@redwood.com.

[14:09] Samir: i want to call out a couple of edge SLOs — cold restart during deployments and long context explosion. we can include these in the risk register.

[14:19] Marcus: Deployment restarts are real for us, thanks.

[14:24] Dana: ok any other open items?
[14:27] Priya: i want to summarize acceptance criteria: weighted p95 and p99 per earlier table, with a pass/fail threshold and mitigation options.
[14:36] Samir: yes we'll put that in the acceptance matrix document; it will include exact formulas and sample-size justification.

[14:46] Lina: last bit — demo we might need for the execs, want a short 15-min demo of the console metrics and fallbacks after bench results?
[14:53] Elliot: yes please.

[15:00] Samir: to close, i'll list deliverables: benchmark scripts + docker image; run schedule with 3 repeats per mode; acceptance matrix; SOC2 and architecture docs; recommended dedicated sizing and cost estimate; spreadsheet for weighted SLO calculation.

[15:18] Lina: action owners and due dates as we discussed: Samir bench artifacts by May 7, Elliot upload traces by May 5, Lina pricing and SOC2 by May 2.

[15:30] Group: thanks everyone.

[15:35] (crosstalk)
[15:38] Priya: one quick ask — please include an example of the route-level dashboard.

[15:43] Samir: will do; i'll attach screenshots in the follow-up.

[15:48] Elliot: great, thanks.

[15:52] Lina: thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and calendar invites for the bench runs.

[15:58] Meeting end notes: duration ~62 minutes.

Artifacts referenced:
- Benchmark plan spreadsheet (to be shared)
- SOC2 report and security architecture diagram (to be attached)
- S3 upload manifest and tokenization tool (link to be provided)
- Acceptance matrix template (sample)

Notes about transcript quality: transcript auto-captures were reasonable but had some mis-heard terms ("KV cash" vs KV cache, "Redwood Dedicate" vs Redwood Dedicated). speaker overlap occasionally labeled generically.

End of transcript.
